Shanghai Municipal Police

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, October 7, 1924.

Sir,

At 4.25 p.m. October 7, D.I.Givens telephoned
from the South Railway Station stating that some of
the Chekiang troops from Sungkiang are reported to
have fallen back along the Railway to Mai Ka Loong
( 杨家弄 ) where they intended to remain
pending further instructions.

Infantry to the number of 500 which arrived
at the South Station from Loongwha to-day intending
to proceed to Wong-doo 王渡 were this afternoon ordered
to proceed immediately "as far as possible"
towards Sungkiang.

At 4.30 p.m. October 7 Magistrate Dung of
the Shanghai Military Court in reply to my question
stated definitely that although heavy fighting
was going on at Sungkiang, the City had not fallen
neither had any of the Chekiang troops stationed at
Sungkiang retreated.

Your Obedient Servant,

J L Dumside
Acting D.C.I.

Acting Commissioner of police.
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处

刑事情报处处长

上海，1924年10月7日。

先生：

10月7日下午4时25分，吉文斯副督察长从南站打来电话，称据报部分来自松江的浙江军队已沿铁路撤退至杨家弄（Mai Ka Loong），并打算在那里停留，等待进一步指令。

今天从龙华抵达南站、原计划前往王渡的500名步兵，于今天下午受命立即“尽可能远地”向松江进发。

10月7日下午4时30分，上海军事法庭法官董先生回复我的询问时明确 stated，尽管松江正在发生激烈战斗，但该城尚未陷落，驻扎在松江的任何浙江军队也未撤退。

您顺从的仆人，

J L Dumside
代理刑事情报处处长

代理警务处处长

Shanghai Municipal Police

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, October 9 1924.

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,

Owing to the cutting early this morning of both
the telephone and telegraph lines between Sungkiang
and the local Military Governor's yamen it is claimed
that no news of to-day's situation has reached Shanghai.

Magistrate Dung confidentially informs me that
within the next day or so he will in all probability
resign his position as a result of being discouraged
in the way that Tuohm Lu Yung Ziang 盧永祥 places
no trust in the staff of General Ho Fung Ling 何豐林.
It is also possible that simultaneously the ex-City
Magistrate Sung Pao Chang 沈保昌 and his brother Sung
Nyi Chang (沈商昌 who have been working day and night
in the office of General Ho will also resign their
positions for the same reason.

The failure of the Chekiang forces defending
Sungkiang is put down to the sending to that sector
of a number of soldiers recently recruited by
Lu Siau Chia 盧筱嘉 who were sent to Sungkiang on
October 7. The recruits commenced "circulating
rumours" which resulted in the defending army becoming
discontented and refusing to fight. The local
General Headquarter Staff upon realising the seriousness
of the situation sent reinforcements to the number of
about 2000. The last batch to the number of 500
under the personal command of General Ho Fung Ling
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处

刑事情报处处长

上海，1924年10月9日。

秘密及机密

先生：

由于今天清晨松江与当地督军公署之间的电话和电报线路均被切断，据称上海方面尚未收到关于今日局势的消息。

董法官私下告知我，鉴于卢永祥对何丰林将军的参谋人员缺乏信任，他感到灰心，很可能在一两天内辞去职务。同样可能的是，前上海县知事沈保昌及其兄弟沈商昌（Sung Nyi Chang），因日夜在何丰林将军办公室工作，也将出于同样的原因辞职。

防守松江的浙江军队失利，归咎于卢筱嘉最近招募的一批士兵被派往该地区，这批新兵于10月7日被送往松江。这些新兵开始“散布谣言”，导致守军不满并拒绝作战。当地总指挥部参谋人员意识到局势的严重性后，派遣了约2000人的增援部队。最后一批500人由何丰林将军亲自指挥

pages.en:
2

left Shanghai this morning and are stated to have
warned all dissenters (mostly belonging to the
39th Regiment) that they would be immediately
shot upon the least sign of refusal of duty.
Besides being short of food and ammunition
another reason for the discontent at present
reigning amongst the defending forces stationed
at Sungkiang is that reinforcements sent from the
Wongdoo王渡 sector were surprised upon learning
the serious plight of the whole of the Chekiang army
whom they had been told were in the ascendancy.
The local Military Authorities admit having heard
such by way of rumour but state that such rumours
"cannot be true".

Your Obedient Servant,
J.C. Burnside
Acting D. C. I.

Acting Commissioner of Police.
（批：OM/1° and B [签名]）

于今晨离开上海，据称他们警告所有异见者（大多属于第39团），一旦 slightest 出现拒绝执行任务的迹象，将立即枪决。
除了缺乏食物和弹药外，目前驻守松江的防御部队中普遍存在不满情绪的另一个原因是，从王渡地区派出的增援部队在得知整个浙江军队陷入严重困境后感到震惊，而他们此前被告知浙江军队占据上风。
当地军事当局承认听到了此类谣言，但声称这些谣言“不可能是真的”。

您顺从的仆人，
J.C. Burnside

Shanghai Municipal Police

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, August 31 1924.

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,

Confidential information from a Nanking Agent
is to the effect that General Tsang Foh Lai 張福來
of Honan had made certain offers to General Ho Fun;
Ling with a view to the latter turning traitor,
failing this, efforts will be renewed to buy over
Colonel Tsu Commander of the Woosung forts.

Further news from the same source is to the effect
that war between Kiangsu and Chekiang is inevitable and
will break out within less than one week. Two reasons
are given for delay, the first being that the troops
of Sun Chuan Fang 孫傳芳 of Fokien are not quite ready
to attack Chekiang. The second reason given is
the efforts for peace of ex-Premier Sun Pao Chi 孫寶琦 who is at present
in Nanking and is expected to arrive in Shanghai on
his way to Hangchow on August 31.

It is further reported that General Chi Hsi Yuan 齊燮元
has made the following three offers to General Lu Yung
Ziang as a basis for peace.

(1) Independence of Chekiang to be abolished.
(2) The Shanghai Military Governor to be under
the command of the Military Governor of Kiangsu.
(3) Immediate disbandment of the troops of General
Chwang Taz Ping 臧致平 and Yang Hwa Tsao 楊化昭

Your Obedient Servant,
J. Burnside
Acting D. C. I.

Acting Commissioner of Police.

刑事情报处处长

上海，1924年8月31日。

秘密及机密

先生：

来自南京特工的机密消息称，河南的张福来将军已向何丰林将军提出某些条件，企图诱使后者叛变；若此计不成，将重新努力收买吴淞要塞指挥官朱司令。

同一来源的进一步消息指出，江苏与浙江之间的战争不可避免，并将在不到一周内爆发。延迟的原因有两个：第一，福建孙传芳的部队尚未完全准备好进攻浙江；第二，前任总理孙宝琦正在进行和平斡旋，他目前在南京，预计将于8月31日在前往杭州的途中抵达上海。

另有报告称，齐燮元将军已向卢永祥将军提出以下三项条件作为和平基础：

(1) 废除浙江的独立地位。
(2) 上海护军使归江苏督军指挥。
(3) 立即解散臧致平和杨化昭的部队

您顺从的仆人，
J. Burnside

Shanghai Municipal Police

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, August 29 192 4.

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,

Upon enquiry at the yamen of the local Military
Governor to day I was informed that generally speaking
there was no change in the present warlike situation.
Both sides were fully prepared for attack and defence
but no reason could be given for delay in opening
hostilities other than the old time slogan "I will
not fire the first shot". It is denied that peace
mediators have any bearing on the present situation.

PEACE PROSPECTS. It is admitted that mediators
for peace are at work and that one party in which is
included the manager of the Bank of Communications
(Sheng Tso Su ) has sent telegrams and delegates
to both the Military Governor of Kiangsu and Chekiang.
On the Chekiang side, General Lu Yung Ziang has already
replied that he will not attack, an answer from General
Chi Hsi Yuan being expected this evening and it is
claimed that on this answer rests the prospects of war.

MAIN ATTACK. It is now claimed by the local
Military authorities that the opening and most probably
main attack on the defenders will take place in the
vicinity of Quinsan, Wusieh and Changchow where General
Chi Hsi Yuan is known is have a force of from 10,000
to 20,000 men.

AEROPLANES. It is stated that both sides are
about equal so far as is known in the matter of aeroplanes
and bombing planes. Most of the flying machines of
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处

刑事情报处处长

上海，1924年8月29日。

秘密及机密

先生：

今天在当地督军公署查询时，我获悉总体而言，目前的战局没有变化。双方都已做好攻防准备，但对于推迟开战的原因，除了老口号“我不开第一枪”外，给不出其他理由。有人否认和平调解人对当前局势有任何影响。

和平前景。有人承认和平调解人正在开展工作，其中一方包括交通银行经理（盛佐苏）已向江苏和浙江督军发送电报并派出代表。在浙江方面，卢永祥将军已回复称他不会发动进攻，预计今晚将收到齐燮元将军的答复，据称战争的 prospects 取决于这一答复。

主要进攻。当地军事当局现在声称，对防御方的首次且很可能是主要的进攻将发生在昆山、无锡和常州附近，众所周知，齐燮元将军在那里拥有10,000至20,000人的部队。

飞机。据称，就已知情况而言，双方在飞机和轰炸机方面的实力大致相当。浙江和上海部队的大部分飞行器

pages.en:
2

the Chekiang and Shanghai forces are said to be
at Hangchow in charge of a Russian. It is
however admitted that the son of Nicholas
Tsu (             ) who saw service in the Great
War in France is one of the prominent aviation
officials on the side of Chekiang and Shanghai.

POISON GAS. The Chekiang and Shanghai forces
stoutly deny that they have any poison gas
and that General Chi Hsi Yuan of Nanking will
not resort to such methods of warfare it being
pointed out that attackers and defenders are
"Brothers and schoolmates". It is, however,
admitted that when this same trouble was on
last year two Germans approached General Lu
Yung Ziang to whom they submitted that they were
in a position to manufacture poison gas and wished
to demonstrate the effects on two dogs, such
proposal being immediately turned down.

RICE SITUATION. The local rice situation
was discussed and according to the local military
Authorities the supply of rice to residents and
refugees will be maintained, it being claimed
that the troops can obtain supplies without
interfering with the local market.

(批：Art / 31/8)
(批：aw / s)

Acting Commissioner of Police.

Your Obedient Servant,
(签名：J.B. Burnside)
Acting D. C. I.
pages.zh:
2

据称都在杭州，由一名俄国人负责。然而，有人承认，尼古拉斯·朱（Nicholas Tsu）（             ）的儿子曾在法国参加大战服役，是浙江和上海方面著名的航空官员之一。

毒气。浙江和上海部队坚决否认拥有任何毒气，并称南京的齐燮元将军不会诉诸这种战争手段，理由是进攻方和防御方是“兄弟和同学”。不过，有人承认，去年发生同样的麻烦时，两名德国人曾接近卢永祥将军，向他们表示有能力制造毒气，并希望用两条狗演示其效果，该提议当即被拒绝。

大米供应情况。讨论了当地的大米供应情况，据当地军事当局称，将维持对居民和难民的粮食供应，并声称军队可以在不影响当地市场的情况下获得补给。

（批注：Art / 8月31日）
（批注：aw / s）

代理警务处处长

(签名：J.B. Burnside)

pages.en:
The Kiangsu-Chekiang-Fukien
Situation

If there were two prominent men in Shanghai who
were enemies, and each had declared his intention
of killing the other at sight, all grant that the situation
would have elements of danger. Then suppose that each
of these men had a number of followers and that
both gangs were armed—armed “to the teeth”—to use
the latest and most approved language of the movie
melodrama, then we would have an interesting situation.
It is pretty difficult for the average person to
imagine such a situation in Shanghai either among
foreigners or among Chinese, but strange as it may
seem, we do have a situation greatly similar to this
in the area immediately outside of the boundaries of
the foreign settlements. We refer to the present
strained political situation between the Chinese pro-
vinces of Kiangsu, Chekiang and Fukien. There isn’t
any particular need explaining the political situation
existing in this part of China, except to repeat what is
already known. The Province of Chekiang just south
of Shanghai is controlled by General Lu Yung-hsiang
who has his headquarters at the city of Hangchow
which is about five hours from Shanghai on the Shang-
hai-Hanchow-Ningpo Railway. The Province of
Kiangsu, in which Shanghai is located is controlled by
General Chi Shih-yuan who has his headquarters at the
city of Nanking about eight hours distant on the Shang-
hai-Nanking Railway and about fifty hours away by
steamer up the Yangtsze. Kiangsu Province with the
exception of a small section surrounding Shanghai is a
so-called “loyal” province in so far as the Central Gov-
ernment at Peking is concerned. Chekiang Province
on the other hand is “independent” of the Peking Gov-
ernment. To the south of Chekiang Province is the
Province of Fukien, which in recent months has become
“loyal” to Peking.
According to the 1923 edition of the China Year
Book the military strength of these three provinces is
as follows: Kiangsu, 79,320 men; Chekiang, 61,875;
Fukien, 84,050. In addition to the armies each of these
three provinces has a “navy” or at least a few gun-boats
of obsolete type, but nevertheless capable of doing some
damage. Two of these provinces Kiangsu and Che-
kiang have recently built up an air-force. Chekiang has
an arsenal which is located at Lungwha on the outskirts
of the French concession of Shanghai. Nanking has no
arsenal, but has a mint which is equally useful. The
only branches of modern-up-to-date warfare lacking in
these war-like preparations are those of poison-gas and
submarines, but possibly these may be added soon for
China is progressing rapidly.
Now with this situation as it is, there is no man in
the world who is in a position to say whether there is go-
ing to be a war in this section of China, or who can say
with any degree of accuracy just when this war is likely
to start. The latest information on the subject is that
General Wu Pei-fu, chief military power behind the
Peking Government has decreed that General Lu Yung-
hsiang of the “independent” Province of Chekiang, be
eliminated. Not one of these generals could
himself tell whether there is to be a war and
if so when it may start. Each general has his
pages.zh:
苏浙闽局势

如果上海有两个显赫人物是死敌，且各自宣称见面即杀对方，所有人都会承认这种局势含有危险因素。再假设这两人各自拥有一大批追随者，且两帮人马都武装到了牙齿——借用最新且最流行的电影情节剧术语——那么我们将面临一个有趣的局面。
普通人很难想象在上海的外国人或中国人中会出现这样的局面，但奇怪的是，在外国租界边界紧邻的区域，我们确实面临着与此极为相似的局势。我们指的是中国江苏、浙江和福建三省之间目前紧张的政治局势。除了重述已知事实外，无需特别解释中国这一地区的政治局势。位于上海正南方的浙江省由卢永祥将军控制，其总部设在杭州，从上海沿沪杭甬铁路前往约需五小时。上海所在的江苏省由齐燮元将军控制，其总部设在南京，沿沪宁铁路前往约需八小时，或乘轮船溯长江而上约需五十小时。就北京中央政府而言，除上海周围一小块区域外，江苏省是一个所谓的“ loyal ”（忠于中央）省份。另一方面，浙江省则“独立”于北京政府之外。浙江省以南是福建省，该省在最近几个月已变得“忠于”北京。
根据《1923年版中国年鉴》，这三个省的军事力量如下：江苏79,320人；浙江61,875人；福建84,050人。除了陆军外，这三个省各自还拥有一支“海军”，或者至少拥有几艘过时的炮艇，尽管如此，它们仍能造成一定破坏。其中两个省，即江苏和浙江，最近建立了空军。浙江拥有一个兵工厂，位于上海法租界郊外的龙华。南京没有兵工厂，但有一个同样有用的造币厂。在这些好战的准备工作中，唯一缺乏的现代最新战争手段是毒气和潜艇，但鉴于中国进步迅速，这些可能很快也会被添加进来。
鉴于目前的局势，世界上没有人能断定中国这一地区是否会发生战争，也没有人能准确预言战争何时可能爆发。关于此事的最新消息是，作为北京政府背后主要军事力量的吴佩孚将军已下令铲除“独立”的浙江省将军卢永祥。这些将军中没有任何一人能亲自断定是否会有战争，如果有，何时开始。每位将军都有他的

pages.en:
his own intelligence officers and the usual quota
of spies and informers inside of the camp of the
other. Every move is reported and exaggerated. If
General Che recruits a dozen soldiers and sends them to
Soochow, the number immediately becomes a hundred
when it is reported in Hangchow. If General Lu sends
a hundred fresh troops to the Shanghai area the num-
ber becomes a regiment when reported in Nanking. If
one of General Che's gunboats which are anchored in
the river at Nanking changes its position, immediately
the report is in circulation that a fleet is coming to
Shanghai to attack General Lu's "independent" navy
and to capture the Shanghai arsenal.
If the situation were not so serious it would be
highly amusing. It reminds one of the old feudal fights
in mediaeval Europe or the fights between the wild
Indian tribes of the North American Continent—or
if we want another simile—it reminds one of some of
recent years for the movies. And it is just about as
sensible as one of these movie extravaganzas.
There is nothing new in the tense political between
Kiangsu and Chekiang. It develops every few months
and when we had the last scare the Chinese General
Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai bestirred itself and
forced the generals of Nanking and Hangchow to sign
a peace pact which was duly published in all the papers.
Each general agreed to keep the peace as long as he
was not "attacked," but herein lies the danger for be-
hind each of these generals are forces which desire an
outbreak of war. Behind General Che is
General Wu Pei-fu who wants to eliminate
General Lu because Lu interferes with the Loyang
General's plan for unification of China by
military force. And behind Lu is General Chang Tso-
ling at Mukden who is opposed to General Wu Pei-fu
and the Peking Government. In addition to this there
are the discordant elements at Canton under Dr. Sun Yat-
sen who are friendly with Chekiang Province and also
opposed to Peking. The schemings and plottings which
are constantly going on in these various military camps
makes the situation highly dangerous and no person of
intelligence would be so rash as to attempt to forecast
what may happen.
As has been emphasised in these columns of The
China Press the most important thing which China
needs right now is peace. The last "war" between
Mukden and Peking plunged the country into chaos and
debt and the fighting around Canton has further
damaged the internal and international status of the
country. A new war in this section of China would be
the most damaging thing that could possibly happen to
the country. In the Shanghai area are concentrated the
great commercial and industrial development of the
country, both foreign and native, and a war here would
be a terrible thing. It would quite likely bring serious
foreign complications and there would be no end to
the trouble.
The price of peace in this section of China is
eternal vigilance on the part of all interests concentrat-
ed here. The foreigners can help a little but the chief
burden rests with the Chinese commercial and finan-
cial interests in Shanghai. The Chinese com-
mercial interests here are in a position to stop this war
before it starts and they can perform this great service
if they will direct the necessary energy and intelligent
thought in that direction.
pages.zh:
自己的情报官员，以及对方阵营中通常数量的间谍和线人。每一个举动都被报告并夸大。如果齐将军招募十二名士兵并将他们派往苏州，当消息传到杭州时，人数立即变成一百人。如果卢将军派遣一百名新兵到上海地区，当消息传到南京时，人数就变成了一个团。如果齐将军停泊在南京河里的一艘炮艇改变了位置，立刻就会有谣言流传，称一支舰队正驶向上海，要攻击卢将军的“独立”海军并夺取上海兵工厂。
如果局势不是如此严重，那将会非常可笑。它让人想起中世纪欧洲的封建争斗，或北美大陆野蛮印第安部落之间的战斗——或者如果我们想要另一个比喻——它让人想起近年来的一些电影情节。而这与那些电影中的荒诞剧一样毫无理智可言。
江苏和浙江之间紧张的政治关系并非新鲜事。这种情况每隔几个月就会发展一次，而在上一次恐慌发生时，上海的中华总商会积极行动，迫使南京和杭州的将军们签署了一项和平协议，该协议随后在所有报纸上公布。每位将军都同意只要不被“攻击”就保持和平，但危险就在于此，因为在每位将军背后都有渴望战争爆发的势力。在齐将军背后是吴佩孚将军，他希望铲除卢将军，因为卢将军妨碍了这位洛阳将军通过武力统一中国的计划。而在卢将军背后是沈阳的张作霖将军，他反对吴佩孚和北京政府。此外，还有广州孙中山博士麾下与浙江省友好且同样反对北京的不和谐因素。这些不同军营中不断进行的阴谋策划使得局势高度危险，任何有识之士都不会鲁莽地试图预测可能发生什么。
正如《字林西报》这些栏目所强调的那样，中国目前最需要的是和平。上次沈阳与北京之间的“战争”使国家陷入混乱和债务之中，而广州周边的战斗进一步损害了国家的国内和国际地位。中国这一地区的新战争将是可能对国家造成的最具破坏性的事情。上海地区集中了国家巨大的商业和工业发展成果，包括外资和本土资本，这里的战争将是一场灾难。这很可能会带来严重的外国纠纷，麻烦将无穷无尽。
中国这一地区和平的代价是所有在此集中的利益相关方保持永恒的警惕。外国人可以提供少许帮助，但主要负担落在上海的中国商业和金融利益集团身上。这里的中国商业利益集团有能力在战争爆发前阻止它，如果他们能将必要的精力和智慧思考导向这一方向，就能完成这项伟大的服务。

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL
Shanghai, August 26 1924.

Sir,

Three military officers attached to the 37th
Regiment 10th Division (Chekiang National Army) stationed
at Kashing and Woochow who attended a military conference
at Loongwha and whose orders are to command the Chekiang
forces in the vicinity of the Taihu Lake state:-

The present garrisons at I-hing 宜興 and Wukiang 吳江
are detached from the 2nd Division stationed at
Soochow. They are not good fighters but may be
re-inforced by a detachment from the 5th Mixed
Brigade stationed at Hsuchow who are under the
command of General Chen Tiao Yuen 陳調元. The 5th
Mixed Brigade comprises the best soldiers of the
Kiangsu forces.

Chekiang will devote all its energies to
overpower the 5th Mixed Brigade of Kiangsu and
should this be successful the immediate fall of
Nanking is a certainty. Although Nanking is
guarded by the 6th Division under the personal
command of General Chi Shih Yuen 齊燮元 and are
known to be well equipped they lack experience.

It is admitted that it would be more
difficult to keep Nanking than to take it but the
main object is to end the career of General
Chi Shih Yuen 齊燮元 than to occupy the City
of Nanking.

? Art

秘密且机密
上海，1924年8月26日。

先生，

驻扎在嘉兴和吴州的浙江国民军第10师第37团的三名军官参加了龙华的一次军事会议，他们的命令是指挥太湖附近的浙江部队，他们表示：

目前驻守宜兴和吴江的卫戍部队是从驻扎在苏州的第2师分遣出来的。他们战斗力不强，但可能会得到驻扎在徐州、由陈调元将军指挥的第5混成旅分遣队的增援。第5混成旅由江苏部队中最优秀的士兵组成。

浙江将全力以赴压倒江苏的第5混成旅，如果成功，南京的立即陷落是必然的。虽然南京由齐燮元将军亲自指挥的第6师守卫，且已知装备精良，但他们缺乏经验。

人们承认，守住南京比攻占南京更困难，但主要目标是终结齐燮元将军的政治生涯，而非占领南京城。

? Art

pages.en:
Military leaders of Chekiang are not giving
attention to the threats of Kiangsu, Anhui
and Fukien. It is pointed out that Kiangsu is
not sincere owing to its Military Governor
being indifferent to Wu Pei Fu 吴佩孚 the Loyang
warlord & Chi Shih Yuen of Nankin. Anhui
is infested with Tufeis and bandits whilst Fukien
has two Generals disagreeing with each other.
That Chang Tso Lin 张作霖 the Manchu warlord
will join with Chekiang in the war is evidenced
by the fact that Chang Tso lin has recently
presented 5000 rifles to Chwang Chi Ping 臧致平 whose
troops have been increased since they were
allowed to enter Chekiang.

浙江的军事领袖们并未对江苏、安徽和福建的威胁给予重视。有人指出，江苏方面缺乏诚意，因为其督军对洛阳军阀吴佩孚或南京的齐燮元态度冷淡。安徽匪患严重，而福建则有两位将军彼此不和。满洲军阀张作霖将与浙江联手参战，这一事实的证据在于：张作霖最近向臧致平赠送了5000支步枪，自臧致平的部队获准进入浙江以来，其兵力已有所增加。

Shanghai Municipal Police

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, August 26 1924.

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,

Information obtained in strict confidence
is to the effect that on the evening of August 24,
a secret conference took place at Loongwha between
Chekiang and Shanghai Generals who decided:-

(1) It was inadvisable to await the opening
of hostilities by Sun Chuan Fang 孫傳芳
of Fokien, and

(2) That Nanking should not be permitted to
complete preparations for war, therefore

(3) Chekiang, who is already prepared, should
take the offensive.

Further information from the same source is that
the outbreak of war between Kiangsu and Chekiang will
take place within one week and that the first clash
will be in the vicinity of Ping Vong 平望 or Wukiang 吳江。

Your Obedient Servant,

[Signature]
Acting D. C. I.

/ Council -

刑事情报处处长

上海，1924年8月26日。

秘密且机密

先生：

通过严格保密渠道获得的情报显示，8月24日晚，浙江和上海的高级将领在龙华举行了一次秘密会议，决定如下：

(1) 等待福建的孙传芳开启战端是不明智的，并且

(2) 不应允许南京完成战争准备，因此

(3) 已经做好准备的浙江方面应采取攻势。

来自同一来源的进一步情报显示，江苏与浙江之间的战争将在一周内爆发，首次冲突将发生在平望或吴江附近。

Shanghai Municipal Police

DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL
INTELLIGENCE

Shanghai, August 23 1924

SECRET & CONFIDENTIAL

Sir,

The local Military Authorities report that there
has been very little change in the Kiangsu-Chekiang
differences since my last visit to the yamen. Detectives
from the yamen reported from the vicinity of Quinsan
that mines had been laid by Chi Hsi Yuen's 齊燮元
men in the vicinity of Tsing Yang Kong 青陽港. near Quinsan -
Soldiers in mufti of Chi Hsi Yuen were reported to be
in vast numbers at Wu-kiang Hsien 吳江縣 and I-hing. 宜興
The Chekiang and Shanghai Authorities are of the opinion
that the soldiers in the vicinity of Quinsan are posted
there as a bait and that their main attack would be
by way of the Tahu Lake and so strike at Kashing,
Fengching and Sungkiang in order to cut off communication
between Shanghai and Chekiang. Such an attack, however,
will not be made until Fokien opens hostilities on the
Chekiang border. Regarding reports in the Foreign Press
of the movement of Chinese men-of-war such are mere rumours
and in any event it is realised that their uselessness
in the present situation is about equal. ^ Dennis -

Your Obedient Servant,

J. B. Burnside.
A/ D. C. I.

Acting Commissioner of Police.

（左侧批注：）

上海，1924年8月23日

秘密且机密

先生：

当地军事当局报告称，自上次拜访衙门以来，江苏与浙江之间的分歧几乎没有变化。来自衙门的侦探从昆山附近报告称，齐燮元的人马在昆山附近的青阳港一带布设了地雷。据报道，齐燮元的便衣士兵大量出现在吴江县和宜兴。浙江和上海当局认为，昆山附近的士兵是被部署在那里作为诱饵，他们的主要进攻路线将是经由太湖，从而打击嘉兴、枫泾和松江，以切断上海与浙江之间的交通。然而，这种攻击只有在福建对浙江边境开启战端后才会发动。关于外国报纸报道的中国军舰调动，这些仅仅是谣言，况且无论如何，人们意识到它们在当前局势下的无用性大致相当。^ Dennis -

您顺从的仆人，

J. B. Burnside.

Summarised translation of a handbill purported
to have been issued by 齊 Chi Shih Yuen's Headquarters
and found in a No.6 tram car. abut Sept 13, 1924.

It accuses General Lu Yung Ziang of having appointed
Ho Fung 何丰林 Military Governor of Sungkiang
and Shanghai without first refering to the Central
Government; of usurping the authority of Kiangsu
in the civil and police administration in 12 Hsiens;
of instigating the murder of Hsu Kuo Liang because
he was opposed to him; of failing to execute his
murderer; of appointing Lu Yung Chien as Chief
of the Woosung-Shanghai Constabulary although the
pay of the Constabulary is provided by the Government;
of harbouring Wong Ah Zau, a tufei leader, who has
several thousand followers and stationing them at
Wushow for the purpose of attacking Anwhui; of
inducing the tufeis in Anwhui to become active;
of bribing the Navy in causing it to secede it from
the Government; of having amassed $20,000,000
through opium smuggling during the past two
years; and of giving refuge to Chang Chi Ping
and Yang Hua Chao.

据称由齐燮元总部发布并于1924年9月13日左右在一辆6路电车上发现的传单的摘要译文。

传单指责卢永祥将军在未先请示中央政府的情况下，任命何丰林为松江和上海护军使；僭越江苏在12个县的民政和警务行政权；因徐国梁反对他而煽动谋杀徐国梁；未能处决谋杀者；尽管巡警队的薪饷由政府提供，仍任命卢永乾为吴淞-上海巡警队队长；窝藏拥有数千名追随者的土匪头目黄阿祖，并将他们驻扎在无锡以图进攻安徽；唆使安徽的土匪活跃起来；贿赂海军导致其脱离政府；在过去两年中通过鸦片走私积累了2000万美元；以及为臧致平和杨化昭提供庇护。

October 24 192 4
REPORT ON Feeding of Troops at Kiangwan
Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.
Sir,
Further to D. I. Sullivan's report dated October 23,
the Chamber of Commerce on October 24 wrote to General Bai Pao
Shan(白寶山) reminding him of his promise to undertake the
feeding of the soldiers at Kiangwan from October 25, and asking
for an answer as to whether he is in a position to do so. Should
a negative reply be received, the Chamber of Commerce will
continue to feed the men as heretofore until other arrangements
are made. There are about nine thousand soldiers in the
vicinity of Kiangwan to whom food costing about $1,500.00
is supplied by the Chamber of Commerce daily.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I.
D. C. I.

Shanghai Municipal Police.

I. O. CENTRAL Station.
October 23 1924

REPORT ON Feeding of troops at Kiangwan

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by [Signature] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

Mr. Fong Tsiao Pah(方椒伯) and Zee Kau Sung
(徐可陞), Vice Chairman and Secretary respectively of the
Chinese General Chamber of Commerce have been interviewed
concerning the supply of food which up to now has been supplied
by the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce for the 9,000 troops
now at Kiangwan. The above gentlemen state that an arrangement
has been come to between General Bai Pao Shan(白寶山), Acting
Military Governor of Shanghai, and the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce for the latter to provide food for the men up to and
including October 24 and that after that date the Acting Military
Governor will undertake to provide for their upkeep.
Mr. Zee Kau Sung(徐可陞), Secretary of the
Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, states that either to-day
or to-morrow General Chang Yun Ming(張之明) and his Hupeh
troops will go north to join the forces of General Wu Pei Fu
and as soon as they have departed the troops now at Kiangwan will
be transferred to Loonghwa and gradually either assimilated
into General Bai Pao Shan's army or sent north.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature] Sullivan.
D. I.

was Oct 25 not Oct 24.

先生：

我们就目前由上海总商会为驻江湾的9000名士兵提供食物供应一事，采访了上海总商会副会长方椒伯先生和秘书徐可陞先生。上述人士称，上海代督军白宝山将军与上海总商会之间已达成一项协议，由后者提供截至10月24日（含当日）的士兵食物，此后日期由代督军负责承担他们的给养。
上海总商会秘书徐可陞先生称，张之明将军及其湖北部队将于今天或明天北上加入吴佩孚将军的部队，一旦他们离开，目前驻江湾的部队将被调往龙华，并逐渐要么被编入白宝山将军的军队，要么被派往北方。

REPORT ON Ex-Military Governor of Sungkiang and Shanghai
and Party.

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

The N. Y. K. S.S. "Kashima Maru" on which
Generals Ho Fung Ling(何豐林), ex-Military Governor of
Sungkiang and Shanghai, and Chwang Tsz Ping(臧致平),
a former General in General Lu Yung Ziang's Frontier
Defence Army were said to be travelling, arrived in Shanghai
from Nagasaki at about 12.45 p.m. October 30 and moored
in midstream opposite the Asiatic Petroleum Co.'s Wharf.
A party of Police in the Police Motor Launch "Pursuit"
awaited the arrival of the vessel. An N.Y.K. passenger
launch also met the ship but there were no Chinese on
board the launch and no sign that any preparations had been
made to meet the two Generals. The passengers who
disembarked were scrutinized and a strict watch kept on
the ship until 3 p.m. Captain Van Tshing Sai(樊青山),
who was a transportation officer attached to Chwang Tsz
Ping's army at the Shanghai North Station and afterwards
in command of the Independent Army at Sungkiang when
that town fell to the Fukien troops, went to the ship in
one of the Shanghai Ferry Service launches. He however,
did not go on board the "Kashima Maru" but stopped on the
launch alongside the liner until about 2 p.m. when he went
away alone in the same launch in which he came and was
landed at one of the jetties in the Yangtsepoo district.
Enquiries were made on board the ship and the purser stated
that three Chinese who gave the names of Wong Yau Tsoo
(黃耀祖), Tseu Zoong Lung(周仲倫) and Woo Lai Tshing

先生：

据说前松江上海护军使何丰林将军和前卢永祥边防军将军臧致平乘坐的日本邮船会社“鹿岛丸”号轮船，于10月30日下午12点45分左右从那霸抵达上海，并停泊在亚洲石油公司码头对面的河中心。一批乘坐警用摩托艇“追击号”的警察等候该船到达。一艘日本邮船会社的乘客接送艇也去迎接该船，但接送艇上没有中国人，也没有迹象表明已做好迎接两位将军的准备。对下船的乘客进行了仔细检查，并对该船保持严密监视直至下午3点。樊青山船长曾是臧致平军队在上海北站的运输官，后来在该镇被福建部队攻陷时指挥松江独立军，他乘坐上海轮渡服务的一艘接送艇前往该船。然而，他并未登上“鹿岛丸”号，而是停留在靠在大客轮旁的接送艇上，直到下午2点左右，他独自乘坐来时的同一艘接送艇离开，并在杨树浦地区的一个码头登岸。经在船上查询，事务长称有三名中国人，报名字为黄耀祖、周仲伦和吴来清

(何梅青) occupied cabin number 34 from Nagasaki to
Shanghai. On going to room number 34 it was found to be
locked and the cabin steward declined to open it saying
that the passengers had gone ashore. The Captain and
Purser were appealed to but would not assist in anyway.
It was not exactly a refusal but a disinclination to
co-operate. Through the agency of a Customs Officer
the cabin was afterwards opened and the three bunks had
every appearance of having been used and two soft felt
hats had been left in the cabin. A Chinese quartermaster
who was questioned stated that a launch came to the ship
from Woosung very early this morning and several Chinese
passengers left the ship and went away in the launch. The
only other information he could give was that he heard a
bargain struck with the launch laodah for $2.00 per
person. The party of Police stayed on the ship until, as
far as could be ascertained, all the passengers had
left the ship and it is certain that during that time the
two generals did not leave. Two minor officials from
the Japanese Consulate went to the ship and the card of
a Japanese Vice Consul was seen on the purser's desk.
This, however, may not have any significance. Two Chinese
detectives were left on board the ship in an endeavour to
find out anything concerning the gentlemen XXX and
arrangements have been made to relieve them at 6 p.m. The
ship is due to leave Shanghai for Europe on November 1 and

December 2 1924
REPORT ON Local Military Situation
Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence.
Sir,
Nothing has happened during the past few days to denote any change in the policy of local military chiefs, and movements of troops, which have taken place in the vicinity of Loonghwa and the Kiangnan Arsenal, are entirely of a local nature without special military significance. Considerable uneasiness has however been occasioned among General Chang Yun Ming and his staff by a report that arrangements were being made for the transfer from Nanking to Shanghai of the 2nd Kiangsu Division, commanded by General Woo Hung Tse (吳恒) to reinforce General Kung Paung Tuh (宮邦鐸).
Chang Yun Ming (張允明), the Hupeh general, denies all knowledge of the report that one of his staff officers had conveyed a request to the railway authorities at the Shanghai (South) Station that all trains traversing the loop line at night should stop at Bridge J.35, and explains that a report seen in the newspapers was the first intimation he had that trenches had been dug near that place. Enquiries which he had instituted on this subject had shown that the trenches were originally dug by General Lu Yung Ziang (盧永祥) but were made broader and deeper by his men who were using them as sleeping quarters. The order for this work had been given without his knowledge by the officer in charge of a party of five hundred men he had dispatched to Sing Loonghwa to protect that district from tufeis. Discontinuance of the use of the trenches had, however, been ordered by General Chang in order to allay rumours. General Chang states that he is at present in control of three mixed brigades distributed as follows :-

November 25 1924

REPORT ON Interview with General Chang Yun Ming

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Director of Criminal Intelligence

Sir,

Det. Insp. Givens and Inter. Zau interviewed
General Chang Yun Ming( 張允明 ) at his yamen in Loonghwa
on the afternoon of November 24. General Chang told the
C.I.D. officers that, in consequence of a telegram received
from Marshal Tuan Chi Jui and other pressure from Peking,
both he and S. K. Chen( 陳世光 ) had decided to assume
officially their respective ppsitions as Defence Commissioner
and Commissioner of Foreign Affairs at Shanghai. Notification
of this decision had on November 24 been sent to eighteen
different foreign consuls in the Settlement. The dispatches
conveying the news, which were delivered personally by
Mr. S. K. Chen, contained an explanation that neither of the
officials assuming office were in possession of the seals
appertaining to their positions, and also stated that new
seals for the incumbent of the Defence Commissionership had
been ordered from Peking. General Chang and his associates
considered that no difficulties were likely to arise in
inducing Mr. Wen Shih Tsung( 溫世珍 ) to hand over the
seals of the Commissioner of Foreign Affairs.

Notwithstanding the challenge to General Kung
Paung Tuh( 宮邦 ) involved in his official assumption of
the office of Defence Commissioner, General Chang does not
anticipate that that incident will cause any change in the
local situation. Whatever the provocation General Chang
intends to remain on the defence, and he does not believe
that General Kung has any intention of attacking him.

关于与张允明将军会谈的报告

报告人：侦探督察 Givens 转呈人：刑事侦缉处处长

阁下，

11月24日下午，侦探督察 Givens 和翻译 Zau 在龙华张允明将军的衙门会见了张允明将军。张将军告诉刑事侦缉处官员，由于收到段祺瑞元帅的电报以及来自北京的其他压力，他和陈世光均决定正式就任上海防卫司令和外交专员职务。11月24日，这一决定的通知已发送给租界内的十八个不同外国领事馆。由陈世光先生亲自递交的传达此消息的公文中解释称，这两位就职官员均未持有与其职位相符的印信，并声明已从北京订购了新任防卫司令的印信。张将军及其同僚认为，促使温世珍先生移交外交专员印信不太可能出现困难。

尽管正式就任防卫司令一职构成了对宫邦铎将军的挑战，但张将军并不认为该事件会导致当地局势发生任何变化。无论受到何种挑衅，张将军打算保持防御姿态，他不相信宫将军有任何攻击他的意图。

REPORT ON Interview with General Chang Yun Ming.

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by C/. Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

General Chang Yun Ming, in an interview on the afternoon of November 17 with Det. Insp. Givens and Interpreter Zau, stated that he claims to be the genuine Military Governor of Shanghai in accordance with his appointment to that position by the Peking Government. General Chang was aware that others, while acknowledging him to be the senior military official in this neighbourhood, were endeavouring to make the general public believe that the rightful successor to the post held by General Ho Fung Ling was General Kung. The latter based his claim to that post on an appointment made by Tuchun Chi of Kiangsu, and the latter's decisions in such matters could always be overruled by the Government. Nevertheless relations between General Chang, General Kung and Tuchun Sun Chuan Fang were cordial, and it was perfectly understood that they would not interfere with each other so long as the present status quo was maintained. According to General Chang's understanding of the status quo, it gave him control of the area South of French Town, including Loonghwa, the Kiangnan Arsenal, the Shanghai (South) Station, the Chinese City, the Nantao Bund and Kao Chang Miao where, however, soldiers belonging to other generals were still stationed. These comprised about 1,000 of General Kung Paung Tuh's troops quartered in the vicinity of the S.H.R. Station (South), 3,000 of Sun Chuan Fang's soldiers stationed in the Kiangnan Arsenal and vicinity, and a company of marines controlled by the Navy

REPORT ON Interview with Prominent Chinese Merchant about
War Situation.
Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by a/ Director of Criminal Intelligence
Sir,
A native of Chekiang, who is one of the most
prominent members of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, was
interviewed on the forenoon of September 22 by D.I. Givens
and Interpreter Zau. This gentleman stigmatized the rumours
that Marshal Lu Yung Ziang could be induced under present
circumstances to discontinue the struggle for monetary
considerations as absolute nonsense, but he thought that it
might be possible to induce him to agree to retire to private
life provided the terms of the bargain condemned Tuchun
Chi Shih Yuan to a similar fate. As proof that Lu could
not be influenced by money, he stated that had the latter
so desired he could have secured a couple of millions taels
before leaving Hangchow, but he was content with a free will
offering of $300,000.00 from the merchants. The expenses
of the war were being paid out of money raised locally by
General Ho Fung Ling, and subsidies from Marshal Chang Tso Lin.
The latter had no less than $2,000,000.00 on deposit in
Shanghai banks, and this entire sum would be at the disposal
of Lu Yung Ziang's party provided they continued the fight.
Four hundred thousand dollars had already been paid, and
the balance would be given in instalments as the struggle
progressed. The war funds at present in possession of
Lu Yung Ziang's party amount to $800,000.00.
In addition to his financial resources, Marshal
Lu has, according to this gentleman, 45,000 loyal troops and
sufficient ammunition in stock to last two months, exclusive

Sir,
Sung Han Chang(宋漢章 ), Manager of the Bank

the notes of the Bank of China in the Province of Chekiang and
district of Shanghai if he failed to comply. He, nevertheless,
refused. A demand for $200,000.00 accompanied by similar
threats addressed to the Bank of Communications has also been
ignored. Other levies which, according to Mr. Sung, the

Chinese General Chamber of Commerce, of which $50,000.00 has
already been paid in cash ; and $100,000.00 from the Shanghai
Electricity and Waterworks Co. which has already been paid.

1924年9月16日
关于浙江军事当局向上海商号和商人征收战争捐税的报告。
由 D. I. Givans 制作 由刑事情报科主任转呈。

先生，
中国银行经理宋漢章于9月16日在接受侦探督察 Givans 和翻译 Zau 的访谈时，证实了浙江当局向他索要500,000.00美元贷款的信息，并威胁如果他不服从，将停止中国银行钞票在浙江省和上海地区的流通。尽管如此，他拒绝了。交通银行也收到了附带类似威胁的200,000.00美元的要求，但该要求同样被无视。据宋先生称，浙江军事当局试图向当地商人征收的其他捐税包括：向南市中华电车公司征收100,000.00美元，这笔款项可能会支付；向华人总商会主席虞洽卿征收2,000,000.00美元，其中50,000.00美元已以现金支付；向上海电力自来水公司征收100,000.00美元，该款项已支付。在上述最后一家公司的董事朱壽永(音译)就资金问题进行谈判期间，曾被拘禁在龙华。这些捐税是通过居住在闸北的许劍青(音译)进行征收的。宋先生认为，除非工部局或领事团采取措施制止浙江当局这种用于筹款的非正规制度，否则上海的商业将会瘫痪。华人圈子里的流言似乎表明目前的
